# `PIXterm` - *draw images in your ANSI terminal with true color*

**`PIXterm`** ***shows images directly in your terminal***, recreating the pixels through a combination of [ANSI character background color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Colors) and the [unicode lower half block element](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_Elements). If image has transparency, an optional matte color can be used for background. Also, you can specify a dithering mode; in which case, the image is rendered using block elements with different shades, or using standard ASCII characters in the same way. In dithering mode, the matte color is used to fill the background of the blocks or characters.

Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF, WebP.

Fetching images from HTTP/HTTPS is supported too.

## Usage

```
pixterm [options] <image file or URL>
```

### Options

- `-version` - show PIXterm version
- `-credits` - show some love to contributors <3
- `-d <mode>` - dithering mode:
  - `0` - no dithering (default)
  - `1` - with blocks
  - `2` - with chars
- `-go` - output Go code to 'fmt.Print()' the image
- `-m <color>` - matte color for transparency or background (optional, hex format, default: 000000)
- `-nobg` - disable background color (optional, only in dithering mode, ignores matte color)
- `-s <method>` - scale method:
  - `0` - resize (default)
  - `1` - fill
  - `2` - fit
- `-tr <rows>` - terminal rows (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 24)
- `-tc <columns>` - terminal columns (optional, >=2; when piping, default: 80)

## Requirements

Your terminal emulator must support *true color* in order to display image colors correctly. In addition, you must use a monospaced font that includes the lower half block unicode character: `▄ (U+2584)`. set -eu

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"unsafe"

	"terminalimage/internal/raster"
)

type options struct {
	mode, scale, rows, cols                int
	matte                                  string
	goCode, noBackground, version, credits bool
}

func usage() {
	name := filepath.Base(os.Args[0])
	if os.Args[0] == "" {
		name = ""
	}
	fmt.Print(banner)
	fmt.Printf(usageText, name)
}
func fail(code int, err error) int {
	fmt.Print(banner)
	log.New(os.Stderr, "[PIXTERM ERROR] ", log.LstdFlags).Print(err)
	return code
}
func terminalSize() (rows, cols int, terminal bool) {
	var ws struct{ Rows, Cols, X, Y uint16 }
	_, _, errno := syscall.Syscall(syscall.SYS_IOCTL, os.Stdout.Fd(), uintptr(syscall.TIOCGWINSZ), uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(&ws)))
	if errno == 0 {
		return int(ws.Rows), int(ws.Cols), true
	}
	return 24, 80, false
}
func parseMatte(s string) (raster.Pixel, error) {
	p := raster.Pixel{A: 255}
	if s == "" {
		return p, nil
	}
	v := s
	if len(v) == 3 {
		v = string([]byte{v[0], v[0], v[1], v[1], v[2], v[2]})
	}
	n, err := fmt.Sscanf(v, "%02x%02x%02x", &p.R, &p.G, &p.B)
	if n != 3 || err != nil {
		return p, fmt.Errorf("matte color : %s is not a hex-color", s)
	}
	return p, nil
}
func load(name string) (*raster.Image, error) {
	var r io.ReadCloser
	if strings.HasPrefix(name, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(name, "https://") {
		response, err := http.Get(name)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		r = response.Body
		if response.StatusCode != 200 {
			r.Close()
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ANSImage: image download failed")
		}
	} else {
		f, err := os.Open(name)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		r = f
	}
	defer r.Close()
	return raster.Read(r)
}
func run(args []string) int {
	var o options
	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("", flag.ContinueOnError)
	fs.SetOutput(io.Discard)
	fs.Usage = usage
	fs.BoolVar(&o.version, "version", false, "")
	fs.BoolVar(&o.credits, "credits", false, "")
	fs.IntVar(&o.mode, "d", 0, "")
	fs.IntVar(&o.scale, "s", 0, "")
	fs.IntVar(&o.rows, "tr", 0, "")
	fs.IntVar(&o.cols, "tc", 0, "")
	fs.StringVar(&o.matte, "m", "", "")
	fs.BoolVar(&o.goCode, "go", false, "")
	fs.BoolVar(&o.noBackground, "nobg", false, "")
	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
		if err == flag.ErrHelp {
			return 0
		}
		return 2
	}
	if o.version {
		fmt.Println("1.3.2")
		return 0
	}
	if o.credits {
		_, _, tty := terminalSize()
		if tty {
			fmt.Print(interactiveCredits())
		} else {
			fmt.Print(banner, creditsText)
		}
		return 0
	}
	if fs.NArg() < 1 || o.mode < 0 || o.mode > 2 || o.scale < 0 || o.scale > 2 || o.rows < 0 || o.rows == 1 || o.cols < 0 || o.cols == 1 {
		usage()
		return 2
	}
	matte, err := parseMatte(o.matte)
	if err != nil {
		return fail(2, err)
	}
	src, err := load(fs.Arg(0))
	if err != nil {
		return fail(1, err)
	}
	rows, cols, tty := terminalSize()
	if o.rows != 0 {
		rows = o.rows + 2
	}
	if o.cols != 0 {
		cols = o.cols
	}
	h, w := (rows-1)*2, cols
	if o.mode != 0 {
		w *= 4
		h *= 4
	}
	switch o.scale {
	case 0:
		src = raster.Resize(src, w, h)
	case 1:
		src = raster.Fill(src, w, h)
	case 2:
		src = raster.Fit(src, w, h)
	}
	src = raster.Composite(src, matte)
	out, err := render(src, o.mode, matte, o.noBackground, o.goCode)
	if err != nil {
		return fail(1, err)
	}
	if tty {
		fmt.Print("\x1b[H\x1b[2J")
	}
	fmt.Print(out)
	if tty {
		fmt.Println()
	}
	return 0
}
func main() { os.Exit(run(os.Args[1:])) }
